note: Fixed copies of case files as hyper held them before a library took their cases, with their caseFiles declarations: fields.json, whose cases http-form holds (F-20 to F-27); redis-sessions.json, whose cases the session-store library holds; and file-store-sessions.json, the cases of contracts/file-sessions.json that the session-store library holds, under another name because contracts/file-sessions.json keeps the cases of hyper. The steps of the three servers read them until the servers call the core, and S-4 removes tests/legacy. Their sentences name the current statements of hyper.

fields.state: `fields` lists the values of `text` as `[name, values]` pairs in the order of their names, or is null when `text` fails with HY-42.

names.state: `names` lists the names of the values of `text` in the order of their first occurrence, or is null when `fields` is null.

fields.state: `fields` lists the form values of the body `body` of the type `type`, a text whose characters are its bytes, as `[name, values]` pairs, or is null when the body fails with HY-42.

files.state: `files` lists the files of the body in request order as objects with `name`, `filename`, `contentType` and `content`, where `content` is the text of the file and `contentType` is empty text for a part without a content type, or is null when `fields` is null.

stopped.state: `stopped` is true when the body `body`, a text whose characters are its bytes, given in chunks of `chunk` bytes, passed a limit, after which no chunk is given.

exceeded.state: `exceeded` is true when the body passed the body limit `limit`, the value limit `valueLimit`, the part limit `partLimit` or the file limit `fileLimit`.

held.state: `held` is the text of the bytes that the body holds as one value: empty text for a body that is read in chunks, which a multipart body of the type `type` is when `stream` is true, and for a body that passed the limit.

fields.state: `fields` lists the form values of the body as `[name, values]` pairs, read from the chunks or from the held bytes, or is null when the body failed or passed the limit.

files.state: `files` lists the files of the body in request order as objects with `name`, `filename`, `contentType`, `content`, the text of the bytes of the file, and `size`, or is null when `fields` is null.

entries.state: `entries` is the number of files in the directory of the body after its last chunk, or null for a body without a directory.

moved.state: `moved` is null when `move` is `none`, and else tells the move of the first file: for `new`, to a path that does not exist, and then a second time; for `exists`, to a path that exists; for `type`, to the number 7. `content` is the text of the bytes at the path after the first move, or of the file when the move failed; `left` is the number of files in the directory after it, or null without a directory; `again` is the message of the failure of the second move or of the failed move; `read` is the message of the failure of `content()` after the move, or null when the move failed; `class` is `value` for the class of HY-46.2 and `type` for TypeError.

removed.state: `removed` is true when the directory of the body does not exist after `remove()`, or null for a body without a directory.

file.state: `content` is a text whose characters U+0000 to U+00FF are bytes; `file` holds what `name()`, `filename()`, `contentType()`, `size()` and `content()` of `new UploadedFile(name, filename, contentType, bytes)` return, the content written as such a text.

results.state: `steps` are run in order on one store over the Redis server in memory of the case, which first holds the keys `keys`, pairs of a key and its bytes as text; `results` holds for each step the results of its calls of `get`, each the value of the data model (HY-44) that it returned, compared as a value, with `null` for no value.

created.state: `created` holds for each step null when the request created no identifier after its close, and `new` when it created 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits that are not the cookie value of the step or an identifier that an earlier step created.

errors.state: `errors` holds for each step null, or the pair of where the first failure happened (`open`, `call` or `close`) and its class: `lock` for `SessionLockError` and `type` for `TypeError`.

commands.state: `commands` are the commands that the server in memory received in order, each the list of its words as text, with `<secret>` for the value of a lock that the store took and `<release>` for the release script.

stored.state: `stored` are the keys of the server in memory after the steps, sorted by key, each a pair of the key and its bytes as text, with `<secret>` for the value of a lock that the store took.

error.state: `error` is part of the message of the error with which making the store with the options `options` fails.

results.state: `steps` are run in order on one store over the temporary directory of the case, which first holds the session files `files`; `results` holds for each step the results of its calls of `get`, each the value of the data model (HY-44) that it returned, compared as a value, with `null` for no value, and of `directory`, the list of file names, or the number that the collection of a `collect` step returned.

created.state: `created` holds for each step null when the request created no identifier after its close, and `new` when it created 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits that are not the cookie value of the step, an identifier of `files` or an identifier that an earlier step created.

errors.state: `errors` holds for each step null, or the pair of where the first failure happened (`open`, `call` or `close`) and its class: `unserialize` for the `UnserializeError` of the php-serialize package and `record` for the `Error` of Node and the `ValueError` of Python.

message.state: `message` is part of the message of the first failure of the case.

records.state: `records` holds for each step the files of the directory after the step, sorted by name, each a pair of its name and its bytes as text whose characters U+0000 to U+00FF are the bytes; the file of the identifier that step n created is named `sess_#n`.

touched.state: `touched` holds for each step the sorted names of the files that `files` gave with an `age` and whose modification time after the step is less than half that age before the start of the case.

error.state: `error` is part of the message of the error with which making the store of the directory `directory`, the temporary directory of the case for `temporary`, with the lifetime `lifetime` fails.

ranges.state: `accept` is the Accept value, or null for a request without it, and `ranges` is the list of its media ranges in order, each with its type and subtype in lower case, its parameters before q as [name, value] pairs with the name in lower case, and its weight in thousandths.

invalid.state: `invalid` is true when the parse refuses the value with the error of an invalid Accept, which the server answers with status 400.

selected.state: `selected` is the type of `types` that the Accept value selects by the weight of its most specific matching range, the first of the highest weight, or null when no type has a weight above 0.

invalid.state: `invalid` is true when the selection refuses the value with the error of an invalid Accept, which the server answers with status 400.

unmaskedBody.state: `unmaskedBody` is the body of the response after each masked value of the token that the session holds after the request is replaced by the text `masked`.

members.state: `members` holds members of the JSON response object by their names, each equal to the member of the body after each masked value of the session token is replaced by the text `masked`.

embedded.state: `embedded` holds members of the JSON value that the element `hy-data` of the document holds, each after each masked value of the session token is replaced by the text `masked`.

bodyCount.state: `bodyCount` lists, for each text of `counted` in its order, how many times the body of the response holds it.

keys.state: `keys` lists the keys of the JSON response object in their order.

sharedKeys.state: `sharedKeys` lists the keys of the member `shared` of the JSON response in their order.

regionKeys.state: `regionKeys` is the names of the regions that the JSON response holds under `regions`, in their order.

tagOfBody.state: `tagOfBody` true states that the `ETag` of the response is `W/"` followed by the first 32 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 digest of its body, with the masked token of the body replaced by the token that the session holds after the request, and `"`.

sameAsEarlier.state: `sameAsEarlier` states, for `tag`, `mask` and `body`, whether the `ETag`, the masked token and the body with its masked values replaced of the response equal those of the response to the request of `before` that `earlier` names.

firstCalls.state: `firstCalls` lists the first calls of the request in the order in which they run, written `action:<route>`, `context`, `shared`, `region:<name>` and `load:<route>`.

handlerCalls.state: `handlerCalls` lists every call of a handler during the request in the order in which the calls start, written as `firstCalls` writes them.

actions.state: `actions` is the number of calls of the actions of the application during the request.

observed.state: `observed` lists, in their order, the pairs of a handler, written as `firstCalls` writes it, and the value that a step `observe` of that handler read during the request.

serviceValues.state: `serviceValues` holds, for each service that the application binds, the members of the service after the request, or null for a service whose factory was not called.

reported.state: `reported` lists the reports that the response hook received during the request, each a pair of the method and the path of its request joined by a space, and the status of its response.

reportedHeaders.state: `reportedHeaders` holds headers of the response that the last report of the response hook received.

notes.state: `notes` are the notes of the reply that the last report of the response hook received, a list of pairs of a name and its value in the order of the first note of each name.

failure.state: `failure` is the failure of the response as the last report of the response hook received it.

failureReported.state: `failureReported` states whether the last report of the response hook received a failure and not null.

elapsedFromStart.state: `elapsedFromStart` true states that the elapsed time of the last report is a number of milliseconds that is not less than the time from the start of the request to the call of `handle` and not more than the time from that start to the return of `handle`, both read by the step on the clock of `handle`, where the start is `request.startedBefore` milliseconds before the call and is given to `handle`, or is the call itself without it.

storedAfter.state: `storedAfter` holds values that the session store holds after the request by their keys, each as a JSON value, and null for a key that the store does not hold.

renewals.state: `renewals` is how many times the request renewed the session.

tokenOfSession.state: `tokenOfSession` true states that the masked token of the response body is a masked value of the token that the session holds after the request.

tokenRenewed.state: `tokenRenewed` states whether the token that the session holds after the request differs from the token that it held before the request.

tokenForm.state: `tokenForm` true states that the session holds 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits as its token after the request.

tokenInBody.state: `tokenInBody` states whether the body of the response holds the token that the session holds after the request.

session.state: `session` false states a request after which the session holds no session token.

storeCalls.state: `storeCalls` lists every call of the session store that the host passes to the application for the request, in order, each written `get <key>`, `set <key>`, `remove <key>` or `renew`; it is empty for a request that opens no session.

logged.state: `logged` lists texts that the log of the server of HY-43.4 holds after the request, of the lines that the server wrote during the request.

restored.state: `restored` true states that a warning of the runtime that the step raises after the request, outside of a request, is not raised as an error.

logCount.state: `logCount` is the number of texts that the server gave to its log of HY-43.4 during the request.

browsers.state: `browsers` lists, for each value that a step `observe` read during the request, in the order of `observed`, one word: `current` for the SHA-256 digest, as 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits, of the 32 bytes of the token that the session holds after the request, `previous` for that digest of the token that the session held when the request was sent, when that token differs, `none` for null, and `other` for every other value.

valueReads.state: `valueReads` is how many times the server enumerated, during the request, the entries of the values of the kind `countingMap` that the handlers of the request returned.

failureLogged.state: `failureLogged` true states that one text that the server gave to its log of HY-43.4 during the request is exactly `hyper: ` followed by the failure that the last report of the response hook received.

openError.state: `openError` is a text that the message of the open error contains.

build.state: `build` is the build id that a `build.json` with the text `text` gives, or null when the file fails; a null `text` is a missing file.

error.state: `error` is `invalid-build` when the file fails with a message that names its path, or null when it gives a build id.

message.state: `message` is a text that the message of the failure of the file contains after its path.

openError.state: `openError` is a text that the message of the open error contains.
